solutions.question: Why is there a need to divide Chemistry into many branches? Give three reasons.
steps: Chemistry has a very wide scope and includes a large number of substances, facts and reactions.
It is difficult to study all the knowledge of Chemistry as one subject; therefore, it is divided into branches for systematic study.
The branches allow people to specialise in particular areas and make the study of Chemistry easier and more useful.
solutions.answer: Chemistry is divided into branches because its scope is very wide, its knowledge is difficult to study as one subject, and specialisation makes its study systematic and useful.

solutions.question: Reactions may take place due to electrons present outside the nucleus or they may take place inside the nucleus. Which branches of Chemistry cover these two types of reactions?
steps: Reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus are studied in Physical Chemistry.
Reactions that take place inside the nucleus are studied in Nuclear Chemistry.
solutions.answer: Physical Chemistry studies reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus, while Nuclear Chemistry studies reactions inside the nucleus.

solutions.question: What types of problems are solved in analytical chemistry?
steps: Analytical chemistry solves problems about the composition of substances.
It identifies the substances or components present (qualitative analysis) and determines their amounts (quantitative analysis).
solutions.answer: Analytical chemistry identifies the components of a substance and determines their amounts.

solutions.question: Both graphite and graphene have hexagonal layered structures. What is the difference?
steps: Graphite consists of many layers of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons, one layer above another.
Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal pattern; it is one atom thick.
solutions.answer: Graphite has many hexagonal carbon layers, whereas graphene is a single hexagonal layer of carbon atoms.

solutions.question: Why are supercritical fluids important?
steps: A supercritical fluid is formed above a substance’s critical temperature and critical pressure.
It has properties of both liquids and gases: it can dissolve substances like a liquid and diffuse through materials like a gas.
These properties make supercritical fluids useful as solvents, for example in extracting substances such as caffeine from coffee.
solutions.answer: Supercritical fluids are useful solvents because they combine liquid-like dissolving ability with gas-like diffusion.

solutions.question: In which state does matter exist in the Sun?
steps: Matter in the Sun exists in the plasma state.
solutions.answer: Plasma.

solutions.question: What is the importance of graphene?
steps: Graphene is a one-atom-thick layer of carbon atoms arranged in a sheet.
It is very strong, light, flexible and transparent, and it conducts electricity very well.
Because of these properties, graphene is useful in electronic devices, touch screens, solar cells and batteries.
solutions.answer: Graphene’s strength, lightness, flexibility, transparency and electrical conductivity make it useful in electronic devices, touch screens, solar cells and batteries.

solutions.question: Which form of matter do most of the material things in this world belong to?
steps: Most material things in the world belong to the solid state.
solutions.answer: The solid state.

solutions.question: How does a supercritical state look like?
steps: A supercritical state is formed when a substance is above its critical temperature and critical pressure.
In this state, the liquid and gas phases become indistinguishable.
It behaves as a fluid with properties intermediate between those of a liquid and a gas.
solutions.answer: A supercritical state is a fluid state in which the liquid and gas phases are indistinguishable.

solutions.question: In what way is plasma created in a fluorescent tube?
steps: A fluorescent tube contains a gas at low pressure.
When a high voltage is applied across the tube, an electric discharge passes through the gas.
The discharge ionizes the gas, producing free electrons and positive ions.
This ionized gas is plasma; it produces ultraviolet radiation that makes the fluorescent coating glow.
solutions.answer: An electric discharge ionizes the low-pressure gas in the tube, creating plasma.

solutions.question: Most of the molecules we study in biochemistry are organic in nature. Where does the difference exist in organic and biochemistry branches of Chemistry?
steps: Organic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with carbon compounds, generally excluding carbonates, bicarbonates and oxides of carbon.
Biochemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with the chemical substances and processes occurring in living organisms.
solutions.answer: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, whereas biochemistry studies the substances and chemical processes of living organisms.

solutions.question: Give the reason of brilliance shown by diamond. Can you improve it?
steps: Diamond has a high refractive index, so light entering it is strongly refracted and undergoes repeated total internal reflection.
This repeated reflection gives diamond its brilliance.
Cutting and polishing diamond into many faces can increase its brilliance by causing more internal reflection.
solutions.answer: Diamond’s high refractive index causes repeated total internal reflection; cutting and polishing it into many faces can enhance its brilliance.

solutions.question: Explain the dissolution of sodium chloride in water.
steps: Water molecules are polar: the oxygen end is partially negative and the hydrogen ends are partially positive.
The partially negative oxygen ends attract Na⁺ ions, while the partially positive hydrogen ends attract Cl⁻ ions.
Water molecules surround and separate the ions from the ionic crystal; this process is called hydration.
The hydrated ions disperse throughout the water: NaCl(s) → Na⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq).
solutions.answer: Polar water molecules hydrate and separate Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions, dissolving sodium chloride.

solutions.question: Why do different compounds have different solubilities in water at a particular temperature?
steps: The solubility of a compound depends on the nature of the solute and the solvent.
It depends on how strongly the solute particles attract one another compared with how strongly they are attracted to the solvent particles.
Different compounds therefore have different solubilities in water at the same temperature.
solutions.answer: Different solute–solute and solute–water attractions give compounds different solubilities in water.

solutions.question: Why NaCl can not be crystallized from water just like KNO₃?
steps: The solubility of sodium chloride changes very little with temperature.
The solubility of potassium nitrate increases greatly as temperature rises.
On cooling a hot saturated solution, much potassium nitrate crystallizes out, whereas little sodium chloride crystallizes.
solutions.answer: NaCl solubility changes little with temperature, unlike KNO₃, so cooling a solution crystallizes much less NaCl.

solutions.question: Why graphite is slippery to touch? Which property of graphite enables it to be used as lubricant?
steps: Graphite consists of layers of carbon atoms.
The forces between these layers are weak, so the layers can slide over one another easily.
This softness and easy sliding make graphite slippery to touch and useful as a lubricant.
solutions.answer: Graphite is slippery because its weakly bonded layers slide over one another; this property enables its use as a lubricant.

solutions.question: Mention the name of the branch of Chemistry in which you will study each of the following topics. Rate of a reaction
steps: Physical chemistry
solutions.answer: Physical chemistry

solutions.question: Mention the name of the branch of Chemistry in which you will study each of the following topics. Digestion of food in human body
steps: Biochemistry
solutions.answer: Biochemistry

solutions.question: Mention the name of the branch of Chemistry in which you will study each of the following topics. Properties of plasma
steps: Physical chemistry
solutions.answer: Physical chemistry

solutions.question: Mention the name of the branch of Chemistry in which you will study each of the following topics. Ecosystem
steps: Environmental chemistry
solutions.answer: Environmental chemistry

solutions.question: Mention the name of the branch of Chemistry in which you will study each of the following topics. Reactions taking place during fireworks
steps: Inorganic chemistry
solutions.answer: Inorganic chemistry

solutions.question: Mention the name of the branch of Chemistry in which you will study each of the following topics. Measurement of the absorption of wavelength with the help of ultraviolet spectrometer
steps: Analytical chemistry
solutions.answer: Analytical chemistry

solutions.question: What are allotropic forms? Explain the allotropic forms of carbon and sulphur. How does coal differ from diamond?
What are supercritical fluids. How are they different from ordinary liquids?
steps: A supercritical fluid is a substance above its critical temperature and critical pressure, where the distinction between its liquid and gaseous states disappears.
Unlike an ordinary liquid, a supercritical fluid has no definite surface between liquid and gas and has no surface tension.
It can diffuse through materials like a gas while dissolving substances like a liquid.
solutions.answer: A supercritical fluid exists above its critical temperature and pressure and combines gas-like diffusion with liquid-like dissolving ability.

solutions.question: Define solubility of a solute. How does the solubility of solutes change with the increase in temperature?
steps: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute, in grams, that dissolves in 100 g of a solvent to form a saturated solution at a particular temperature.
The solubility of most solid solutes increases with an increase in temperature.
The solubility of gases in liquids generally decreases with an increase in temperature.
solutions.answer: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in 100 g of solvent to form a saturated solution at a particular temperature. It generally increases for solids and decreases for gases as temperature rises.

solutions.question: What types of movements are present in gaseous and liquid molecules?
steps: Molecules in liquids and gases possess translational, vibrational and rotational motions.
solutions.answer: Liquid and gaseous molecules have translational, vibrational and rotational motions.

solutions.question: Differentiate between the areas which are studied under inorganic and organic chemistry.
steps: Inorganic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with all elements and their compounds, except organic compounds.
Organic chemistry is the branch of chemistry that deals with hydrocarbons and their derivatives.
solutions.answer: Inorganic chemistry studies elements and their compounds other than organic compounds; organic chemistry studies hydrocarbons and their derivatives.

solutions.question: Preparation of solutions leads to an important process in chemistry which enables us to purify a compound through crystallization. Describe a process in which potassium nitrate is purified by crystallizing it in water.
steps: Dissolve the impure potassium nitrate in the minimum amount of hot water.
Filter the hot solution to remove insoluble impurities.
Allow the filtrate to cool. Potassium nitrate crystals form because its solubility decreases as the solution cools.
Separate the crystals by filtration, wash them with a little cold water and dry them.
solutions.answer: Potassium nitrate is purified by dissolving it in hot water, filtering, cooling the filtrate to form crystals, and then separating, washing and drying the crystals.

solutions.question: Graphene is called a miracle material and it is the material of the future. Which of its many properties makes it very useful in electronics?
steps: Graphene has very high electrical conductivity.
Its electrons can move freely through its structure, making it useful in electronic devices.
solutions.answer: Graphene’s very high electrical conductivity, due to freely moving electrons, makes it useful in electronics.

mcqs.stem: Matter is present in neon signs in the state of:
rationales: A supercritical fluid exists above its critical temperature and pressure, not ordinarily in neon signs.
Neon signs contain ionized neon gas, which is plasma.
Neon is a gas before it is ionized, but the glowing matter in an operating sign is plasma.
Liquid crystals have properties intermediate between liquids and crystalline solids and are not the matter in neon signs.

mcqs.stem: Hazardous effects of shopping bags are studied in:
rationales: Geochemistry studies the chemical composition and processes of Earth materials, not the environmental effects of shopping bags.
Inorganic chemistry focuses on compounds generally outside organic chemistry, rather than the environmental hazards of bags.
Analytical chemistry is concerned with identifying and measuring substances, not primarily with their environmental effects.
Environmental chemistry studies the effects of pollutants and waste, including hazards associated with shopping bags.
Starch is a naturally occurring polymer made by plants.
Polystyrene is a synthetic, man-made polymer.
Proteins are naturally occurring polymers made from amino acids.
Cellulose is a naturally occurring polymer found in plant cell walls.

mcqs.stem: The crystals of which substance has rhombic shape?
rationales: Brass is an alloy and does not form the characteristic rhombic crystals asked about here.
Sulphur can form rhombic crystals, known as rhombic sulphur.
Graphite crystallizes in a layered hexagonal structure rather than a rhombic one.
Bronze is an alloy and is not the substance with rhombic crystals.

mcqs.stem: Which liquid among the following is a colloidal solution?
options: Slaked lime used for white wash
rationales: Milk is a colloid in which fat droplets are dispersed through water.
Slaked lime used for whitewash is a suspension of solid particles in water.
Vinegar is acetic acid dissolved in water, forming a true solution.
Silver chloride is insoluble in water and forms a suspension or precipitate rather than a colloidal solution.

mcqs.stem: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
options: A solution of calcium hydroxide in water
A solution of potassium nitrate in water
rationales: Calcium hydroxide dissolved in water forms a solution that is homogeneous in the dissolved portion.
Potassium nitrate dissolved in water forms a homogeneous solution.
Hot chocolate may contain dispersed particles, but concrete is the clearly heterogeneous mixture among these choices.
Concrete is heterogeneous because its components, such as cement, sand, and aggregate, remain distinct and unevenly distributed.

mcqs.stem: A state of matter whose properties are between those of liquids and crystalline solids:
rationales: Liquid crystals have properties intermediate between those of ordinary liquids and crystalline solids.
A supercritical fluid is a substance above its critical temperature and pressure, not the state defined here.
Plasma is an ionized gas and does not have the stated intermediate properties.
Dark matter is a proposed form of matter in astrophysics, not this state of matter.

mcqs.stem: When the tiny visible particles of a substance are dispersed through a medium, the mixture is named as:
rationales: A true solution has particles too small to be visible and does not show visible dispersed particles.
Colloid particles are small and generally cannot be seen individually with the naked eye.
A suspension contains dispersed particles large enough to be visible.
A saturated solution is defined by containing the maximum dissolved solute at a given condition, not by visible dispersed particles.

mcqs.stem: A solution of KClO₃ has a solubility of about 13.2g per 100 cm³ at 40°C. How its solubility will be affected, if you decrease the temperature?
options: The solubility will remain the same
The solubility will first increase with temperature and then it will decrease
rationales: For potassium chlorate, lowering the temperature generally lowers its solubility in water.
The solubility of potassium chlorate decreases as the temperature is lowered.
Its solubility does not remain constant when temperature changes.
The solubility does not first increase and then decrease as temperature is lowered over the conditions described.

mcqs.stem: You are studying the rate of hydrolysis of starch under different conditions of temperature. In which branch of chemistry this topic will fall?
rationales: Organic chemistry studies carbon compounds, but the focus here is the rate of a process under changing conditions.
Analytical chemistry concerns determining the composition or amount of substances, not primarily reaction rates.
Biochemistry studies chemical processes in living organisms, whereas this question focuses on reaction kinetics under different temperatures.
Physical chemistry includes chemical kinetics and the study of how temperature affects reaction rates.
